## Purpose and instructions

Explain which unit outcomes are assessed, what resources may be used, and how
learners should record reasoning. This is integrated practice, not a collection
of minimally varied lesson exercises.

## Part A: concepts and conditions

Use explanation, counterexample, classification, or assumption-checking tasks.
Require mathematical justification, not keyword recall.

## Part B: manual reasoning

Use multi-step problems that combine at least two lessons. Ask learners to show
the governing result, intermediate work, domain restrictions, and a check.

## Part C: computation and interpretation

Use computation because it reveals structure, tests a conjecture, or scales a
method—not merely to repeat arithmetic. Require a prediction before code and an
interpretation after it.

## Part D: synthesis

Include one unfamiliar problem in which the learner must choose and defend a
method. A valid solution may compare symbolic, numerical, or graphical routes.

## Solutions and rubric

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Complete solutions"}
Provide step-by-step solutions, alternative methods where instructive, common
failure modes, and explicit verification. Map each problem to its outcome and
skill mode.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### Reflection

Ask learners to identify which errors were conceptual, procedural,
computational, or interpretive, then link targeted review lessons.
:::
